phases.name: Harvest path — connector spill to cache to coverage ledger (harvest skill scope; merge/xlsx-target-sheet excluded)

steps.name: Namespaced dedup key strategies (core/dedup.mjs)
criteria: canonicalKey(sourceId, id) produces a namespaced key of the form '<sourceId>:<id>', verified indirectly once linkedin.dedupKey wraps it in step 01-03
fuzzyKey(sourceId, company, title, location) produces a namespaced fallback key with case normalised, whitespace collapsed, and punctuation stripped, per DR-0006 rule 3
two different sourceIds never collide on the same underlying id (verified by the 'two sources can never collide...' scenario)
steps.scenario_name: a canonical LinkedIn job id produces a key prefixed "linkedin:"
steps.implementation_notes: dedup.mjs is pure and has zero DIRECT unit coverage. Its only coverage is indirect, through linkedin.dedupKey in source-registry.test.mjs — those two scenarios only go GREEN once step 01-03 (linkedin.mjs) wraps canonicalKey. fuzzyKey's normalisation behaviour has NO test at all, direct or indirect (feature-delta.md gap G2) — implement strictly to the DR-0006 prose and flag for a fast-follow DISTILL pass adding a direct dedup.test.mjs.

steps.name: Slim raw payloads and quarantine schema drift (core/slim.mjs)
criteria: a well-formed spill payload slims to a record with quarantine: null and record: non-null
the slimmed record has exactly the keys date, id, plaintextBody, sender, snippet, subject — cache/fixture shape parity
a digest body shorter than MINIMUM_DIGEST_BODY_LENGTH (1024) quarantines with reason BODY_TOO_SHORT and record: null
a digest body with no /jobs/view/ advert link quarantines with reason NO_ADVERT_LINK even when long enough
boundary: length MINIMUM_DIGEST_BODY_LENGTH - 1 quarantines; exactly MINIMUM_DIGEST_BODY_LENGTH with a link does not
a quarantined result's quarantine payload carries the original message id, for correlation with a human review queue
steps.scenario_name: slims a well-formed digest payload with no quarantine
steps.implementation_notes: No dependency on any other in-scope module. This is the DR-0003/Q5 mitigation for the one drift mode DR-0003 does not fully close (truncated-but-parsable spill payloads).

steps.name: Source registry and LinkedIn descriptor
criteria: REGISTRY is a first-match-wins array whose first entry is the linkedin descriptor (id 'linkedin')
linkedin.matches(message) is true for sender jobalerts-noreply@linkedin.com, false for an unrelated sender
selectSource(message, REGISTRY) returns the matching descriptor, or null when nothing matches
linkedin.extract(message) always returns an array — a 3-job digest extracts 3 rows; a 1-job alert extracts an array of length 1 (no shape field, per DR-0006)
extractAll(messages, REGISTRY) captures every message matching no descriptor in an Unmatched bucket (id + sender), never dropping it, while still returning rows for matched messages
linkedin.dedupKey(rawJob) produces a key namespaced 'linkedin:<id>' by delegating to dedup.mjs's canonicalKey
steps.scenario_name: selects the linkedin descriptor for a LinkedIn message
steps.implementation_notes: linkedin.extract wraps the existing src/core/parse-linkedin.mjs unchanged (Reuse Analysis, feature-delta.md) — no parsing logic is rewritten here, only wired behind the descriptor. linkedin.dedupKey composes dedup.mjs's canonicalKey('linkedin', jobId), completing the two indirect dedup scenarios deferred from step 01-01. This test file has 10 individual it() cases across REGISTRY/matches/selectSource/extract/extractAll/dedup — grouped into 6 criteria here; flagged as a candidly large step in the handoff report.

steps.name: Coverage interval algebra (core/coverage.mjs)
criteria: validateInterval refuses with CoverageRefusal.INVERTED_INTERVAL when `to` precedes `from`; accepts a well-formed interval and a single-day interval where from === to
mergeIntervals([]) returns []; overlapping intervals merge into one; day-adjacent intervals merge into one; non-adjacent intervals stay separate; unordered input returns sorted output
an empty window (messageCount: 0) still merges and is retained as covered, never re-offered

subtractCoverage returns [] when the window is fully covered, the whole window when nothing covers it, and only the remaining gap for a partially covered window; non-contiguous backfill leaves the untouched middle as a single gap in ascending order
nextUncoveredWindow returns the first uncovered sub-window when several gaps exist, null when the request is fully covered, and null for a window covered only by a zero-message-count interval
steps.scenario_name: returns the first uncovered sub-window when several gaps exist
steps.implementation_notes: This file has 16 individual it()/it.each cases across four functions (validateInterval, mergeIntervals, subtractCoverage, nextUncoveredWindow) grouped into 5 criteria above by function rather than enumerated — flagged as oversized in the handoff report. The it.skip('@property ...') case at the bottom is a deliberately deferred PBT placeholder (no fast-check installed) and is out of scope for this step; do not un-skip it.

steps.name: Coverage ledger adapter with fail-closed probe
criteria: store.read() on an absent ledger file returns [] without error
store.probe() refuses with LedgerRefusal.UNREADABLE on a truncated or invalid-JSON ledger file, and leaves the corrupt file byte-identical — never a silent reset
store.commit(interval) refuses with LedgerRefusal.INVERTED_INTERVAL when `to` precedes `from`
store.commit(interval) refuses with LedgerRefusal.NOT_WRITABLE when the ledger directory is not writable
steps.scenario_name: an absent ledger file reads as empty coverage — not an error
steps.implementation_notes: commit() merges the new interval into the persisted set via core/coverage.mjs's mergeIntervals/validateInterval (DR-0002 storage layout). This test file ALSO contains 4 TargetSheet scenarios (createTargetSheet from src/adapters/xlsx-target-sheet.mjs) — those are OUT OF SCOPE this run (merge/xlsx-target-sheet excluded per user decision) and are expected to remain RED after this step. Do not implement createTargetSheet here.

steps.name: Month-sharded message cache writer
criteria: messageCache.put(record) writes a slimmed record under cacheRoot/<YYYY-MM>/<id>.json, sharded by the record's own date (DR-0002 storage layout)
put() applied through a successful ingest grows cache.messageIds by exactly the number of newly ingested, non-duplicate records
messageCache.probe() refuses with CacheRefusal.NOT_WRITABLE when cacheRoot is not writable
steps.scenario_name: coverage does NOT commit when the count check passes but --complete is absent
steps.implementation_notes: message-cache.mjs has no dedicated test file of its own; its writes are observed indirectly through the CLI-level state-delta assertions in ingest-fail-closed.test.mjs (cache.messageIds growth/unchanged). No acceptance scenario in scope directly exercises CacheRefusal.NOT_WRITABLE on this adapter — implement per the scaffold's declared contract and flag for a fast-follow direct adapter test. No dependency on slim.mjs or raw-spill-source.mjs: this module only ever receives an already-slimmed record as a parameter.

steps.name: Raw spill directory adapter with window/count checks
criteria: refuses (surfaced by the CLI as a window violation) when a spilled message's date falls outside the declared window — SpillRefusal.OUTSIDE_WINDOW
refuses, naming the offending file, on a spill file that is not valid JSON — SpillRefusal.NOT_JSON
refuses, naming the offending file, on a spill file missing plaintextBody — SpillRefusal.MISSING_BODY
a spill directory holding fewer files than --expect is surfaced as a count mismatch, not silently accepted
a duplicate id already present in the cache is skipped silently during list/read and still counts toward the expected count — resumability, not an error (DR-0002)
steps.scenario_name: @error refuses when an ingested message falls outside the declared window
steps.implementation_notes: Exercised only via the CLI subprocess in ingest-fail-closed.test.mjs — there is no direct unit test file for raw-spill-source.mjs. Depends on core/slim.mjs (step 01-02) for the quarantine path referenced in the module's own header comment (DR-0003/Q5), even though quarantine itself is not asserted as a distinct SpillRefusal code in this test file — slim's quarantine and this adapter's SpillRefusal codes are separate, complementary checks (structural validity here; semantic truncation in slim).

steps.name: CLI ingest and plan-fetch subcommands (composition root: wire, probe, use)
criteria: `harvest ingest --raw <dir> --window <a>..<b> --expect <n>` refuses with a named reason in stderr and unchanged cache/ledger state for: out-of-window message ('window'), count mismatch ('count'/'expect'), a non-JSON spill file (names the file), a spill file missing plaintextBody (names the file)
`harvest ingest ... --complete` commits coverage only when the count check passes; without --complete, the cache grows but ledger.coverage stays unchanged
`harvest ingest ... --expect 5 --complete` against fewer actual files refuses outright and commits nothing, not even partially
a duplicate id already cached is skipped silently and still satisfies --expect, exiting 0 with ledger.coverage grown by exactly one
the composition root wires ledger-store, message-cache, and raw-spill-source and probes each before doing any ingest work; a failed probe refuses to start
steps.scenario_name: a duplicate id already cached is skipped silently and counts as satisfied — resumability, not an error
steps.implementation_notes: The existing `--in/--out` walking-skeleton invocation (walking-skeleton.test.mjs, 8/8 green) must keep working unmodified — do not touch that code path. `harvest build` (merge.mjs + xlsx-target-sheet.mjs) is OUT OF SCOPE this run: all 3 scenarios in dry-run.test.mjs, and the 4 TargetSheet scenarios in probe-contracts.test.mjs, are expected to remain RED after this step — do not attempt to make `build` succeed or implement createTargetSheet/planMerge. `plan-fetch` has zero direct acceptance coverage in this suite (feature-delta.md gap G1) — implement it per DR-0002 (reads coverage.mjs + the cache via nextUncoveredWindow, prints the next uncovered window, writes nothing) relying on coverage.test.mjs's indirect coverage of the underlying algebra; flag for a fast-follow CLI-level test.

steps.name: Harvest Claude Code skill — thin courier, no record content
steps.scenario_name: rule 2: loops plan-fetch, fetch, ingest until plan-fetch reports full coverage
criteria: Valid frontmatter; invokes only plan-fetch/ingest via approved control-value flags; never opens, quotes, or extracts spill/cache content; treats message ids as fetch hints only, never keys.
Loops plan-fetch, fetch, ingest until plan-fetch reports full coverage — no other stopping condition.
Stages each window's newly spilled mcp-*-get_message-*.txt files, by path, into a fresh per-window directory passed as --raw.
Queries Gmail with after:/before: UTC-midnight epoch-second bounds, never YYYY/MM/DD dates, and fetches with messageFormat: FULL_CONTENT.
Stops the window without --complete and reports when a fetch returns inline; otherwise passes --complete only once every page is exhausted and --expect equals the fetched count.
steps.implementation_notes: test_file is no longer null: DISTILL wrote tests/acceptance/job-alert-harvester/harvest-skill.test.mjs (12 structural rules, committed c89127f, review-approved). The test is structural because the skill is agent-executed prose, not code — each rule asserts a fact about .claude/skills/harvest/SKILL.md's content rather than exercising running code. Rule 1 (frontmatter) already passes against the scaffold; rules 2-12 are RED and drive this step's GREEN work, per DR-0003 (thin-courier discipline: no record content, ids as fetch hints only) and DR-0007 (spill contract: per-window --raw staging of mcp-*-get_message-*.txt files, UTC-midnight epoch-second Gmail bounds, FULL_CONTENT fetch, hard stop without --complete on an inline result). Depends on 01-10: the skill must name the spill directory and file pattern (`mcp-*-get_message-*.txt`) the adapter actually reads, not the invented `.json` shape.

steps.name: Adapter reads the real harness spill contract (DR-0007)
criteria: Spill file selection matches only mcp-*-get_message-*.txt; every other file in the directory is ignored, never counted toward --expect
A candidate file's JSON is read as the message itself — no {result} wrapper is unwrapped or expected
Refusals distinguish not-json, not-a-message, and missing-plaintext-body, each naming the offending file
slim keeps exactly the six cache keys (date, id, plaintextBody, sender, snippet, subject), dropping the harness's extra keys
A real spill fixture, copied byte-for-byte from the harness, ingests end to end: cache grows by one, coverage commits
steps.implementation_notes: Newly RED scenarios for this contract span spill-contract.test.mjs, slim.test.mjs, ingest-fail-closed.test.mjs, and tests/integration/job-alert-harvester/raw-spill-source.test.mjs (the last still encodes the invented .json/{result} shape in 3 of its 7 tests — including asserting payload.result.id — and is owned by this step, per docs/feature/job-alert-harvester/distill/red-classification.md § 2026-09-13 session). The CLI (src/cli/harvest.mjs) needs no change. See docs/feature/job-alert-harvester/distill/red-classification.md for the full newly-red set and root causes.

steps.name: plan-fetch offers one UTC day; skill ingests its window (DR-0002)
criteria: plan-fetch prints only the earliest uncovered UTC day in the requested range, never the whole gap
a day covered by a zero-message-count interval is never re-offered
coverage is filtered by --source: another source's committed coverage never counts toward this source's gap
plan-fetch refuses an inverted --from/--to range instead of reporting full coverage
the skill's ingest --window is exactly the window plan-fetch printed, never the requested --from/--to range
steps.scenario_name: offers only the first uncovered day, not the whole gap, when the ledger is empty
steps.implementation_notes: RED set (docs/feature/job-alert-harvester/distill/red-classification.md § 2026-09-14 session): 5 of the 7 plan-fetch.test.mjs scenarios (line 36 'offers only the first uncovered day...', line 54 'offers the next day...', line 73 'skips a day covered by a zero-message interval...', line 112 'coverage committed for a different source...', line 150 '@error refuses a range where --from is later than --to'), plus harvest-skill.test.mjs rule 13 (line 196 'ingest --window is exactly the window plan-fetch printed, never the requested range'). The 2 remaining plan-fetch.test.mjs scenarios (line 92 'reports full coverage, with no window offered...', line 131 'writes nothing to the workspace...') already pass — keep them green, do not touch their behaviour. Window sizing is domain logic and belongs in core or the CLI, never in the skill (DR-0003, agent couriers paths, never records): whether coverage.mjs gains a one-day-cap function or src/cli/harvest.mjs caps nextUncoveredWindow's result before printing is the crafter's call. coverage.test.mjs's existing multi-day nextUncoveredWindow scenarios are unchanged and must stay green — nextUncoveredWindow itself is not being narrowed to one day, only what plan-fetch prints from its result. The inverted-range refusal (DR-0002: refuses malformed intervals) is a second, distinct bug fixed in this same step via validateInterval, already exercised on ingest but not yet wired into plan-fetch. The skill change (.claude/skills/harvest/SKILL.md) is a single --window correction — replace the requested-range placeholder with the window plan-fetch's own output returned — plus supporting prose; it introduces no new domain logic, per DR-0003 thin-courier discipline. STRUCTURAL VERIFICATION (mandatory, plugin/skill) applies only to the SKILL.md prose change; the coverage.mjs/harvest.mjs CLI change is application code and is covered at the CLI port by plan-fetch.test.mjs (Vitest). This is a JavaScript project with no property-based testing library installed (fast-check is deliberately absent), so no new test framework is introduced.

steps.name: merged coverage intervals report the summed message count (DR-0002)
criteria: merging two day-adjacent intervals produces one interval whose messageCount is the sum of the two merged messageCounts
merging two overlapping intervals also sums their messageCounts, not just the day-adjacent case
merging an interval with messageCount 0 into another contributes zero and preserves the other side's messageCount exactly
steps.scenario_name: merging adjacent intervals sums their message counts
steps.implementation_notes: Defect found by the live Phase 3.5 gate on 2026-09-14: 2026-09-10 (messageCount 5) merged with 2026-09-11 (messageCount 6) produced one interval reporting messageCount 5 while covering 11 cached messages — coverage decisions read only from/to so no mail was skipped, but DR-0002 justifies intervals partly on coverage being inspectable, and the ledger's figure was wrong. User decision 2026-09-14: a merged interval reports the sum of the counts it absorbs. mergeIntervals is pure and the fix is confined to it; completedAt on a merged interval is out of scope for this step. The existing mergeIntervals scenarios for overlap, adjacency, ordering and the empty case must stay green.
